Hello,

I will post in this thread my apps which are useless except for understanding and/or explaining some basic Shiny functioning.

library(shinyAce)
showfiles <- function(){
  list(
    aceEditor("server",
              value = paste(readLines("server.R"), collapse="\n"),
              mode="r", theme="cobalt", height="260px",
              readOnly=TRUE),
    aceEditor("ui",
              value = paste(readLines("ui.R"), collapse="\n"),
              mode="r", theme="cobalt", height="400px",
              readOnly=TRUE)
    )
}

Hey everyone!  In the process of getting up and running with Shiny and shiny-server, I put together a project that simplifies things by giving you access to a fully running virtual machine with R, shiny, and the shiny-server all installed and configured.  You can find the project here:

https://github.com/mdagost/vagrant_shiny

It uses vagrant for managing the virtual machines and puppet for doing the provisioning.  The puppet recipe can be easily re-used if you're managing deployments of Shiny apps to various server environments.  There are branches for both Ubuntu and Debian.

Feel free to reach out to me with any comments or issues.  Hope someone else finds this useful.

Michelangelo

messages.subject: Re: app dependencies on other packages
messages.subject_clean: app dependencies on other packages
messages.body_plain:
Well, a shiny app is just a collection of R scripts, therefore you could do something like...

if(!require(FOO)) {install.packages("FOO",repos="http://cran.us.r-project.org");require(FOO);}

The only problem is that if a user runs your app via runUrl() or something without knowing what they're getting into, you'll be installing software on their local machine without their explicit permission. You could put a button into your app that installs the missing packages if the user signals agreement by clicking it. Alternatively, you could have the app output a message like... "This app needs the following packages: FOO, BAR, BAZ in order to function. To get the normal app functionality instead of this message, please install these packages or ask the administrator of this server to do so."

Hi all,

I've managed to get Shiny running on Heroku.  See http://shiny-example-2.herokuapp.com/.  It's not all roses yet.  Details:
The repository for that app is at https://bitbucket.org/btubbs/shiny-example-2.  Feel free to clone and hack on it.
I forked virtualstaticvoid's existing heroku-buildpack-r, updated it to 3.0.2, took out the building via Vulcan and just used a shell from "heroku run /bin/bash" to rebuild R myself.  The resulting buildpack is at https://github.com/yougov/heroku-buildpack-r.  The R build script is in support/build-r in that repo.
I'm just using Shiny, not Shiny Server.  So to make this work you have to opt your app into the public beta of Heroku's websockets feature. See https://blog.heroku.com/archives/2013/10/8/websockets-public-beta.
The app seems to go to sleep after a minute or two of inactivity (a gray overlay covers the page).  I'm not sure if that's a limitation of doing Websockets through Heroku or if they're just putting the dyno to sleep because I'm at the free single-instance tier.  I might try running under shiny-server to work around that.
I've compiled X11 support into R, but it seems that getting graphics to work requires an X server to actually be running, which Heroku doesn't have.  To demonstrate, I've put up an app with the first example from the tutorial at http://shiny-example-1.herokuapp.com/.  The graph fails to appear, with the error "unable to start device PNG" in red.  A look at the logs shows that it's dying when trying to contact an X11 display.  See http://pastie.org/8451506.
Is there a way to get R to generate PNGs without needing an X server running?

Thanks,
Brent

messages.subject: Re: Uploading data
messages.subject_clean: Uploading data
messages.body_plain:
I used reactive values. Useful if you want users to change the data (e.g., remove variables). In global.R I specify values <- reactiveValues(). The relevant function is listed below. You can see it in action at:

http://vnijs.rady.ucsd.edu:3838/marketing/

loadUserData <- function(filename, uFile) {

  ext <- file_ext(filename)
  objname <- sub(paste(".",ext,sep = ""),"",basename(filename))
  ext <- tolower(ext)

  if(ext == 'rda' || ext == 'rdata') {
    robjname <- load(uFile)
    values[[objname]] <- data.frame(get(robjname))  # only work with data.frames
  }

  if(length(values[['datasetlist']]) == 0 || values[['datasetlist']][1] == '') {
    values[['datasetlist']] <- c(objname)
  } else {
    values[['datasetlist']] <- unique(c(objname,values[['datasetlist']]))
  }

  if(ext == 'sav') {
    values[[objname]] <- as.data.frame(as.data.set(spss.system.file(uFile)))
  } else if(ext == 'dta') {
    values[[objname]] <- read.dta(uFile)
  } else if(ext == 'csv') {
    values[[objname]] <- read.csv(uFile, header=input$header, sep=input$sep)

  }
}

Hello, I have just taken a look at sliderInput. We can look what happens in the html code generated by sliderInput() : > > wrap_ui <- function(x){ > cat(as.character(x)) > } > > wrap_ui(sliderInput("mu0", HTML("H0") > ,min = 1,max = 100,value = 40, step=0.5)) >
> > >
The problem is that the label losts its html attribute because of the as.character() function at the beginning: > > sliderInput > function (inputId, label, min, max, value, step = NULL, round = FALSE, > format = "#,##0.#####", locale = "us", ticks = TRUE, animate = FALSE) > { > labelText <- as.character(label) > ........... > tags$div(tagList(controlLabel(inputId, labelText), slider(inputId, > min = min, max = max, value = value, step = step, round = round, > locale = locale, format = format, ticks = ticks, animate = animate))) > } > A possible solution is to modify the controlLabel() function appearing at the end : > > shiny:::controlLabel > function (controlName, label) > { > tags$label(class = "control-label", `for` = controlName, > label) > } Replacing label with HTML(label) should work. messages.subject_clean: reactivity question
messages.body_plain:
On Mon, Nov 4, 2013 at 7:08 AM, Stéphane Laurent <lauren...@yahoo.fr> wrote:

> I have understand the mystery :)
>
> This is due to the following piece of code:
>
>     factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
>     Factors <- unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors])
>
> ... which is reactive to every input !
>
> Problem solved now:
>
>     factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
>     Factors <- isolate(unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors]))
>

Yes, using reactiveValuesToList is discouraged for this very reason. In addition to "regular" input values, there are some input values that can change when you don't expect it, such as when the browser window is resized, and sometimes the hover position of the mouse over an image, so using reactiveValuesToList can result in your app doing way too much work. The function was previously called as.list.reactiveValues, but we renamed it to make it more difficult for people to turn the entire input object into a list and thus take a dependency on all input values.

At any rate, you might be better off with something like this:

factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)

Factors <- unlist(lapply(factors, function(x) input[[x]]))

Or even better, use vapply (you may have to replace the `character(1)` with the the appropriate type):
vapply(factors, function(x) input[[x]], character(1))

-Winston

messages.subject: Shiny buildpack for Heroku (now with images)
messages.subject_clean: Shiny buildpack for Heroku (now with images)
messages.body_plain:
Thank you to those who offered suggestions to my problem of images not working in my Heroku Shiny environment.  It turned out to be a combination of Cairo not being compiled in to my custom build or enabled in .Rprofile.

Those things are now fixed, and you can see a running sample app, with images, at http://shiny-example-1.herokuapp.com/.

I've also packaged up a Shiny-specific buildpack, so you can deploy an app to Heroku with just a ui.R and server.R in your repository.  See https://github.com/btubbs/heroku-buildpack-shiny.

I'm more a devops hacker than an R expert, so there may be subtleties to the R environment that I'm oblivious to and that still aren't quite right.  Let me know if you find any.

messages.subject: Re: Google Analytics tracking code
messages.subject_clean: Google Analytics tracking code
messages.body_plain:
I generally put a defintion of Google Tag Manager (http://www.google.com/tagmanager/)  in global.R, then write that out as HTML where I want it in ui.R.  This way you can alter the tracking using the GTM interface without changing the code in Shiny again.

So in global.R I have something like this:

GTM <- "<!-- Google Tag Manager -->

<noscript><iframe src=\"//www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-XXXXX\ <http://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-XXXXX%5C>"

height=\"0\" width=\"0\" style=\"display:none;visibility:hidden\"></iframe></noscript>
<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
'//www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id='+i+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f) <http://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id='+i+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f)>;

})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-PCVW');</script>

<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->"

...the GTM container tag as defined by the GTM interface.

Then add to where you want it in ui.R by:

    div(id="GTM", HTML(GTM))

Then login to GTM and activate Universal Analytics, event listeners etc.

Hope that helps,
Mark

messages.body_plain:
That sounds like a smart work around, but RJSONIO does not seem to
support literal symbols, e.g. RJSONIO::toJSON('foo') gives a quoted
string ["foo"], and there is no way to generate foo. I think that is
why Ramnath used a special character string "#! foo !#" to "protect"
the symbol, and restore it later. There is only a limited number of
data types supported in the conversion between R and JSON data.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <yi...@rstudio.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

One thing I've read is that shiny server maintains the websocket connection between itself and the shiny app, so people interacting with shiny server don't have to be using websockets.  So shiny server ought to support users on IE9 and earlier, while using this buildpack would not.

Heroku's websocket support is in beta.  I've noticed that if you visit http://shiny-example-1.herokuapp.com/ and leave it alone for a while, a translucent gray overlay covers the screen and you need to refresh the page before you can interact with it again.  I don't know if this is a quirk in Shiny itself or in Heroku's websockets implementation (which is in beta).

messages.subject: Debugging button hint for shiny development
messages.subject_clean: Debugging button hint for shiny development
messages.body_plain:
I've been off-list for a while, so this sort of thing may be common knowledge, but here's a simple trick discovered by a bay area programmer to make debugging easier:

 <https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/-t2mSFTAmyJo/UnmXeBfIezI/AAAAAAAAAXc/yDz49uObFJg/s1600/Screen+Shot+2013-11-05+at+5.11.56+PM.png> => Browse[1]>

When you are debugging or authoring a shiny application in RStudio or the console, debugging often means you have to add 'browser()' somewhere to the code and restart your application - which may lose state.

Here's how to add a button that drops back to the R console (or RStudio console) in the context of the server.

You can then run most code from your reactives (not any UI stuff) to find out why it's breaking.

When you are done, type c<enter> to resume your shiny app.

It keeps any objects you create from one click (and session) to the next.

In server.r:

  observe(label="console",{
    if(input$console != 0) {
      options(browserNLdisabled=TRUE)
      saved_console<-".RDuetConsole"
      if (file.exists(saved_console)) load(saved_console)
      isolate(browser())
      save(file=saved_console,list=ls(environment()))
    }
  })

In ui.r (in the sidebar or top bar perhaps):

        actionButton("console","server console"),

-Alex

Reproducible example which handles text as input.

server.r
library(shiny)
options(encoding = "utf8")

# Define server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  datasetInput <- reactive({
  input$char
  })
})

ui.r
library(shiny)
# Define UI
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
# Application title
headerPanel("Test input characters"),
sidebarPanel(
textInput("char", "Write character", "")
),
mainPanel()
))

>
> You can then run most code from your reactives (not any UI stuff) to find out why it's breaking.

>       isolate(browser())
>       save(file=saved_console,list=ls(environment()))
>     }
>   })

messages.body_plain:
I apologize in advance that I am not providing reproducible code. But I hope my question can be answered as a more general one.

I have a 'ui.r' file and 'server.r' code that work (see the relevant parts of it below). But here is what my question is about.
As you can see, there is nothing in 'bigone' below that is isolated. There is isolation happening under 'renderPlot'.
However, when I start testing - BEFORE I even start making any input selections, I get an error message in red on my main Panel in Chrome:

Error: Attention: You have to upload the input files starting with your utils!

So, it looks like for some reason Shiny starts evaluating everything under shinySever even before I hit my 'Run' button (goButton).
How can I prevent Shiny from doing anything until I hit my goButton?
Thanks a lot!

Dimitri

############################################################################
# IN MY 'server.r' CODE I HAVE:

shinyServer(function(input,output){

  # Defining the big thing 'bigone' that calculates everything based on inputs provided:

  bigone<-reactive({

    inFile1<-input$utils                # one of my inputs in ui.r has the name 'utils'
    if(is.null(inFile1)) stop("Attention: You have to upload the input files starting with your utils!")
  ...
  ...
  ...
    result<-list(medians=mymedians, ...,  ...)
    return(result)  # code end; return list with 3 elements
  })

  # Creating a plot:
  output$medians.plot1 <- renderPlot({
    input$goButton
    # Isolating:
    isolate(
      print(ggplot(bigone()$medians,aes(x=reorder(att_levels, WTP), y=WTP)) +
        .........      )
    )
  })

})

############################################################################
# IN MY 'ui.r' CODE I HAVE:

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title:
  headerPanel("My Application"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select the inputs:

  sidebarPanel(

    fileInput('utils','Upload your file with utils:'),                      # input is called 'utils'
     ...
     ...
    actionButton("goButton","Run")
  ),

  # Define Main Panel (with tabs):

  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Plot1",  plotOutput("medians.plot1",height="600px")),
    tabPanel("Plot 2", plotOutput("medians.plot2",height="600px"))

    )
  )
))

Dear all,

I'm very new to shiny and am experimenting a number of features with a view to incorporating them into a bigger project.

The idea is that the user may enter the number of tabPanels AND rename them.

I've been able to make the number of tabPanels using Ramnath's code here (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19470426/r-shiny-add-tabpanel-to-tabsetpanel-dynamicaly-with-the-use-of-renderui).

But I've been far less succesful trying to allow the user to rename the tabs. I copy my flawed attempt below: all tabs are renamed simultaneously with names like "Case 1", "Case 2", etc. rather than separetely with unique names as in "Case of the Rue Morgue", "Case of the dog in the nighttime", etc..

I'd appreciate suggestions!

Thanks:

library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/anonymous/7369572")

# server.R

library("shiny")

shinyServer(

  function(input, output, session){

    output$myInput = renderUI({
      nInput = input$nInput
      name = input$name
      myInput = lapply(paste(name, 1: nInput), tabPanel)
      do.call(tabsetPanel, myInput)
    })

    output$myName = renderUI({numericInput("name", 'Name', "Case")})

  }
)

# ui.R

shinyUI(

  pageWithSidebar(

    headerPanel('Dynamic Tabs')
    ,
    sidebarPanel(
      numericInput("nInput", 'Number of Cases', 1)
    )
    ,
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput('myInput')
      ,
      uiOutput('myName')
    )
  )
)

On Saturday, September 14, 2013 3:19:53 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

> MM2, it has to do with connections where websockets cannot be successfully used. Shiny Server uses SockJS which provides a websocket-like interface that is either implemented using actual websockets if possible, and if not, then it falls back to emulating websockets using older technologies such as XmlHttpRequest.
>
> We tag each SockJS connection with a unique token, this is for security related reasons that are not really worth getting into. If we see a given token more than once, previously we were rejecting the second and subsequent attempts to use the token. But in your cases the token was legitimately getting sent >1 times because the websocket was partially but not fully successful--it succeeded enough to redeem the token but not enough that SockJS considered the connection usable. So the fix I implemented is to allow tokens to be reused.

The input file can be under a different directory; the output is
strongly recommended to be under the current working directory. So you
can do something like

input = normalizePath('foo.Rmd')  # full path

out = knit2html(input, output = tempfile(, '.'))

file.copy(out, file)

messages.subject_clean: Shiny - input/output text with trema / diaeresis
messages.body_plain:
I'm no expert on character encodings, but I suspect the problem is that Windows isn't displaying UTF-8 correctly. Character encoding in R is generally difficult on Windows.

The UTF-8 encoding for ë is c3 ab in hex, which is equivalent to 195 171. If you try to print them out, you see different things on Mac and Windows (or at least, that's what I got):
  rawToChar(as.raw(c(195, 171)))
  # [1] "ë"      # Mac
  # [1] "Ã«"     # Windows

You can use iconv to convert encodings. On Windows (for me), this prints out "ë":
  iconv(rawToChar(as.raw(c(195, 171))), from="UTF-8", to="ISO8859-1")
  # [1] "ë"

So maybe what's happening is that the values are sent over as UTF-8, and if you want them to display properly in Windows, you need to convert with iconv.

-Winston

>   df
> })

Dear all,

I have a quite obvious question, but I could not find the answer on the Internet.

I would like to use the value the user inserts in the Shiny app to determine how many new numericInput() fields have to be created in the next step. To be more concrete, in the first step the user enters the number of effect sizes he/she wants to insert in the app and in the next step this number of numeric fields are created.

Preferably I would like to use something like this in the UI:

    conditionalPanel(
      numericInput("nstudies", "Number of studies", value = 2),
      rep(numericInput("COR", "Raw correlation coefficient", value = 0), nstudies))

However, this does not work and I do not know how I should specify the object in the rep() function that I called nstudies.

Is it possible in the way I propose or is there a workaround for this issue?

Thank you in advance,
Robbie

messages.body_plain:
Michael,

I think your issue is related to your inability to clone GitHub repos. I haven't seen that before (other than momentary hiccups in GitHub's availability), so I'd bet there's a firewall issue. The problem is that you're unable to complete the 'npm install' step since you can't get all the dependencies. We've been talking about restructuring a piece of the project that would eliminate this issue for you. Until that's finalized, you'll need to find a work-around to get the npm dependencies.

If you have access to another OpenSUSE system not behind that firewall, you could try installing there and then copying the 'node_modules' directory over to your current machine. It would need to be a similar architecture to your existing machine, though, as some code will be compiled that might be incompatible if you were on a different OS/architecture. Perhaps your last option would be to get the node_modules using npm on another machine (not behind the firewall, perhaps with a different OS or architecture) then use node-gyp <https://github.com/TooTallNate/node-gyp> to compile for your own platform.

Sorry this is pretty messy -- we haven't encountered this scenario before so this isn't too well supported. If we are able to whip up a formal solution I'll mention it here and be sure to add it to the wiki.

messages.body_plain:
The plot works correctly outside the reactive context, and the subsetting seems to be working correctly using renderVerbatimText().

The applet is at http://vanderplas.dyndns-remote.com/Shiny/SoybeanApp/

I've created a reproducible example here:

ui.R
library(shiny)

# Define UI for page that allows selection of genetic lines with corresponding facets
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Soybean Copy Number Variants"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    helpText("Choose the varieties and chromosomes you would like to display CNVs from"),
    uiOutput("VarietyList"),
    uiOutput("ChromosomeList"),
    submitButton("Update View")
  ),

  # Show a plot of the relevant chromosomes and varieties
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("ChromosomePlot"),
    verbatimTextOutput("DebugText")
  )
))

server.R:
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Reproducible example
segranges.df2 <- data.frame(
  seqnames=rep(c("A", "B"), each=10),
  start=rep(c(1:10), times=2),
  end=rep(c(2:11), times=2),
  Variety="1",
  count=rnorm(20, 32, 4)
)

res.df <- data.frame(
  seqnames=rep(c("A", "B"), each=2),
  start=c(1, 3, 5, 9),
  end=c(2, 4, 6, 10),
  Variety="1"
)

# Define server logic required to generate and plot a subset of varieties with a subset of chromosomes
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$VarietyList <- renderUI({
    varieties <- sort(unique(res.df$Variety))
    checkboxGroupInput("varieties", "Choose Varieties", varieties)
  })

  output$ChromosomeList <- renderUI({
    chrs <- unique(res.df$seqnames)
    checkboxGroupInput("chromosomes", "Choose Chromosomes", chrs)
  })

  # Expression that generates a plot of the distribution. The expression
  # is wrapped in a call to renderPlot to indicate that:
  #
  #  1) It is "reactive" and therefore should be automatically
  #     re-executed when inputs change
  #  2) Its output type is a plot
  #
  output$ChromosomePlot <- renderPlot({
#     ggplot() +
#       geom_text(data=unique(subset(segranges.df2,
#                             seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
#                             Variety%in%input$varieties)[,c(1, 3)]),
#                 aes(x=seqnames, y=Variety, label=Variety))
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data=subset(segranges.df2,
                            seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                            Variety%in%input$varieties),
                aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-.5, ymax=.5,
                    fill=count, colour=count)) +
      scale_fill_gradient("# Reads", trans="log",
                          low="#FFFFFF", high="#000000",
                          breaks=c(1, 20, 400, 8000, 160000),
                          na.value="#FFFFFF") +
      scale_colour_gradient("# Reads", trans="log",
                            low="#FFFFFF", high="#000000",
                            breaks=c(1, 20, 400, 8000, 160000),
                            na.value="#FFFFFF") +
      geom_rect(data=subset(res.df,
                            seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                            Variety%in%input$varieties),
                aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-.6, ymax=.6),
                fill="green", colour="green") +
      facet_grid(Variety~seqnames, scales="free") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(axis.text.y=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.y=element_blank(),
            axis.title.y=element_blank())

  })

  output$DebugText <- renderPrint({
    print(input$chromosomes)
    print(input$varieties)
    head(subset(res.df,
                seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                Variety%in%input$varieties))
    head(subset(segranges.df2,
                seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                Variety%in%input$varieties))
  })
})

The applet is at http://vanderplas.dyndns-remote.com/Shiny/SoybeanApp/

I've created a reproducible example here:

ui.R
library(shiny)

# Define UI for page that allows selection of genetic lines with corresponding facets
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Soybean Copy Number Variants"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    helpText("Choose the varieties and chromosomes you would like to display CNVs from"),
    uiOutput("VarietyList"),
    uiOutput("ChromosomeList"),
    submitButton("Update View")
  ),

  # Show a plot of the relevant chromosomes and varieties
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("ChromosomePlot"),
    verbatimTextOutput("DebugText")
  )
))

server.R:
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Reproducible example
segranges.df2 <- data.frame(
  seqnames=rep(c("A", "B"), each=10),
  start=rep(c(1:10), times=2),
  end=rep(c(2:11), times=2),
  Variety="1",
  count=rnorm(20, 32, 4)
)

res.df <- data.frame(
  seqnames=rep(c("A", "B"), each=2),
  start=c(1, 3, 5, 9),
  end=c(2, 4, 6, 10),
  Variety="1"
)

# Define server logic required to generate and plot a subset of varieties with a subset of chromosomes
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$VarietyList <- renderUI({
    varieties <- sort(unique(res.df$Variety))
    checkboxGroupInput("varieties", "Choose Varieties", varieties)
  })

  output$ChromosomeList <- renderUI({
    chrs <- unique(res.df$seqnames)
    checkboxGroupInput("chromosomes", "Choose Chromosomes", chrs)
  })

  # Expression that generates a plot of the distribution. The expression
  # is wrapped in a call to renderPlot to indicate that:
  #
  #  1) It is "reactive" and therefore should be automatically
  #     re-executed when inputs change
  #  2) Its output type is a plot
  #
  output$ChromosomePlot <- renderPlot({
#     ggplot() +
#       geom_text(data=unique(subset(segranges.df2,
#                             seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
#                             Variety%in%input$varieties)[,c(1, 3)]),
#                 aes(x=seqnames, y=Variety, label=Variety))
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data=subset(segranges.df2,
                            seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                            Variety%in%input$varieties),
                aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-.5, ymax=.5,
                    fill=count, colour=count)) +
      scale_fill_gradient("# Reads", trans="log",
                          low="#FFFFFF", high="#000000",
                          breaks=c(1, 20, 400, 8000, 160000),
                          na.value="#FFFFFF") +
      scale_colour_gradient("# Reads", trans="log",
                            low="#FFFFFF", high="#000000",
                            breaks=c(1, 20, 400, 8000, 160000),
                            na.value="#FFFFFF") +
      geom_rect(data=subset(res.df,
                            seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                            Variety%in%input$varieties),
                aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-.6, ymax=.6),
                fill="green", colour="green") +
      facet_grid(Variety~seqnames, scales="free") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(axis.text.y=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.y=element_blank(),
            axis.title.y=element_blank())

  })

  output$DebugText <- renderPrint({
    print(input$chromosomes)
    print(input$varieties)
    head(subset(res.df,
                seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                Variety%in%input$varieties))
    head(subset(segranges.df2,
                seqnames%in%input$chromosomes &
                Variety%in%input$varieties))
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: /var/shiny-server/www vs./srv/shiny-server on EC2
messages.subject_clean: /var/shiny-server/www vs./srv/shiny-server on EC2
messages.body_plain:
The 0.4.0 versions of Shiny Server look for the apps in /srv/shiny-server, while older versions (0.3.x and earlier) look for them under /var/shiny-server/www. Sorry for the inconvenience, but /var/ was simply the wrong place to put it, and we though it better to fix the problem before we hit 1.0.

If you uninstall what you have now and install from the new .deb installer then it should take care of both problems for you. Please read these instructions on upgrading <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#upgrading-from-shiny-server-0.3.5> first, as it's important that you uninstall the old shiny-server and upgrade the Shiny package.

messages.subject: Re: tcltk package
messages.subject_clean: tcltk package
messages.body_plain:
tcltk won't work with Shiny on the server, since tcltk will be trying to launch windows on the server which is almost certainly not what you want, even if it worked.

For message boxes, you could do something with custom messages, like this:

Add this to ui.R, somewhere inside your UI (doesn't matter where):
  tags$script("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('messageBox', function(msg){window.alert(msg);})")

Then whenever you want to send a message in server.R, use this (change "Hello!" to any string):
  session$sendCustomMessage("messageBox", "Hello!")

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Thank you for the Shiny package! In my opinion it is very useful. However, I experience some difficulties.

I would like to combine the input the user gives in a vector. Depending on the input of the user I create a number of "numericInput" fields, so the user can choose to enter 2 but also 20 values. In the next step, I want to combine these inputs in a vector to use further on in the analyses.

My code:

  output$dyn_input <- renderUI({
    inputs <- lapply(1:input$n, function(i) {
      input_name  <- paste("Correlation study", i, sep=" ")

      numericInput(input_name, label = input_name, value = 0, min = -1, max = 1)

      })

    do.call(tagList, inputs)
  })

input$n refers to the number of "numericInput" fields.

Of course I can combine the input with: "object <- c(input$"Correlation study 1", input$"Correlation study 2")" in case of only two values entered by the user, but this becomes problematic when the user enters for instance 10 values.

A highly similar question was asked before (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/3KEjXnW1oWY), but without replies.

Thank you in advance for your help!

messages.subject_clean: Converting Shiny UI to HTML5 UI
messages.body_plain:
There is no "tool" that I know of but it can be achieved (for most simple apps).

The steps are as follows
In Chrome right click and then click on View page source (perhaps other users can help fill in this step for other browsers)
Copy the content of the newly opened page into the file www/index.html
Remove your ui.R (or rename it to something else for backup purposes)
Now your folder structure should look like
server.R
www
index.html
Run your Shiny app using runApp(...) as you normally would.

Jeff

messages.subject: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart
messages.subject_clean: tipsy tooltips on a d3 chart
messages.body_plain:
Hey Folks,

Once again, thanks so much for shiny, and for gracefully dealing with my inane questions! I must make the usual apology and disclaimer that I'm very woefully inexperienced with every piece of technology which I'm trying to use.

I'd like to make a scatter chart in d3, with tooltips that contain links. I'd like to bind events to the links, so that the app might whisk the user to a new tab with some more detailed information on the data point in question.

So far I've got to a minimal Frankenexample from Jeff's nets <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/tSUCaJr4OFE>, and Kenton's Bars <https://github.com/timelyportfolio/shiny-d3-accordion-portfolio>, with the addition of jdonaldson's tipsy tooltips <http://bl.ocks.org/jdonaldson/1193712>.

I've fallen at the first hurdle, which is making tipsy render svg titles when the visual is hosted via shiny. I can get it going on a static page (here <https://rawgithub.com/brendan-R/shiny-d3-scatter/master/static_example/index.html>, ignore the nonsense labels).

Via shiny, the svg elements do have the right titles as defined in d3 (in the usual postit coloured boxes), but they don't have controllable tipsy behaviours or styles. My instinct was that the tipsy css/js wasn't loading (as far as I can tell from looking at my browser's GET requests, it is), or that a tiny bit of js (to set and 'activate' the tipsy options) wasn't running (I tested this by defining a variable inside it, and seeing if it was retrievable from my browser, which it was).

So, my guess is that either the reading of the tipsy js, css, or the in-code .js which sets it's options <https://github.com/brendan-R/shiny-d3-scatter/blob/master/graph.js#L29-39> are being read in the wrong place. Unfortunately I have no idea where the right place is. Currently they're read in as part of graph.js. Attempts to get it between <head> tags have killed the app altogether.

Hopefully this is trivial to someone who understands the DOM... Any ideas?

Brendan

P.S.
The app's on GH <https://github.com/brendan-R/shiny-d3-scatter> ( runGitHub("shiny-d3-scatter","brendan-R") ).

I've been using Shiny at work for a couple months now. The combination of R and web interaction is helping me move multiple tasks out of spreadsheets. So, first, kudos to the dev team.

The current app I'm developing presents results in the form of a table. Right now, it's a gvisTable, though it could be a standard Shiny Table or DataTable if the solution requires it.     output$checkbook <- renderGvis({

messages.subject_clean: How to control text wrap/row height and fixed columns in a table (custom html/css styling)?
messages.body_plain:
Try putting this right before htmlOutput("checkbook"):

tags$style(type="text/css",
  HTML("#checkbook td:first-child { min-width: 200px }")
)

That should format the first column. 200px means 200 pixels.

To do the same for the second column, change "td:first-child" to "td:first-child+td", and for third column, you'd use "td:first-child+td+td", etc.

Pretty hokey, but I didn't see a nicer way to control widths with gvisTable.

messages.body_plain:
It looks like your R processes are crashing before Shiny Server can connect, or some other failure to connect is occurring.

Are you attempting to use a custom Shiny application? I'd recommend trying first with one of the "hello world" examples that comes with shiny (in /examples/01_hello", for instance). You can also check the logs in your log directory (/var/log/shiny-server/) by default to see if you get any more insight about why an application would be crashing.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: How to control text wrap/row height and fixed columns in a table (custom html/css styling)?
messages.subject_clean: How to control text wrap/row height and fixed columns in a table (custom html/css styling)?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, that worked great. Had no idea what syntax to use to apply custom rendering to a Shiny element.

The white-space: nowrap property also works, for the case when a known pixel value may be too limiting. Easy enough to apply to the entire table as well. Ex:

tags$style(type="text/css", HTML("#checkbook td { white-space: nowrap }"))

Can anyone offer insight on how to do a frozen lefthand column similar to this example: http://jsfiddle.net/emn13/YMvk9/. I'll continue playing around a bit with different property settings, but so far all I've gotten is a very ugly result.

On Thursday, November 14, 2013 7:44:56 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Try putting this right before htmlOutput("checkbook"):
>
> tags$style(type="text/css",
>   HTML("#checkbook td:first-child { min-width: 200px }")
> )
>
> That should format the first column. 200px means 200 pixels.
>
> To do the same for the second column, change "td:first-child" to "td:first-child+td", and for third column, you'd use "td:first-child+td+td", etc.
>
> Pretty hokey, but I didn't see a nicer way to control widths with gvisTable.

messages.body_plain:
Sure thing. Here <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/d9d961b521839aa68e946d8ade0fd05f1f3962e8/README.md> is the old README and the wiki pages <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/_pages> are still available for Ubuntu and CentOS install instructions, if you had used any information from either of those.

Sorry for the headache with 0.4.0. We're working to expand the footprint of supported distributions. Hopefully we'll go through the process of getting SLES supported before long to save you some trouble in the future.

One afterthought -- I've noticed some connectivity problems with npm this week (from which you would have been downloading various packages). In fact, when I went to get the link for the shiny server 0.3.6 module (here <https://npmjs.org/package/shiny-server>), the site was down. I can't imagine that it would have consistently caused you as much trouble as you've seen this week, but it's worth keeping in mind. Certainly keep an eye out for that if you encounter any issues installing 0.3.6 -- it's still down for me right now.

Best,
Jeff

messages.subject: shinyIncubator matrixInput with colnames alignment problem
messages.subject_clean: shinyIncubator matrixInput with colnames alignment problem
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm just starting to play around with the matrixInput function of the shinyIncubator package, and it's a great tool!

By default, matrixInput does not show the colnames. I have figured out how to display them by tweaking the tags, but I cannot 1) align the vertical separator and 2) center the colnames inside the cell.

An example is here:

library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/anonymous/7488653")

You can see in the css tags$style below that I have been able to 'un-hide' the colnames and to center text inside table cells for all except the un-hidden colnames. There is also a (possibly related) weird problem of alignment of the vertical separator. The vertical separator for colnames is squeezed to the left, while the vertical separator for the rest of the input table is squeezed to the right.

Suggestions appreciated, thanks!

# ui.R

library("shiny")
library("shinyIncubator")

# initialize data with colnames
df <- data.frame(matrix(c("0","0"), 1, 2))
colnames(df) <- c("first", "second")

shinyUI(
  pageWithSidebar(

    headerPanel("Alignment Problem Inside matrixInput")
    ,
    sidebarPanel(

      # customize display settings
      tags$head(
        tags$style(type='text/css'
          , ".data {background-color: rgb(255,255,255);}" # make inside of cells white
          , ".table th, .table td {text-align: center;}" # works except for colnames
          , ".tableinput .hide {display: inline; width:100%}" # un-hide colnames
        )
      )
      ,
      matrixInput(inputId = 'data', label = '', data = df)
      ,
      helpText(h4("I have added colnames to the initial dataframe and unhidden them with display option inside the class 'hide'. Unfortunately they are not aligned and I can't figure out which option to tweak. I would like to align and center the data columns with the column of colnames."))
    )
    ,
    mainPanel()
  )
)

# server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {})

messages.subject: feedback to R through Shiny
messages.subject_clean: feedback to R through Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have seen a few different ways to see feedbacks work with shiny.. most noticibly in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/ITFUwvYE-f8

I wanted to see what is the latest and best method for doing so. Concretely, here is what I want to do -

1 - Have an input variable on client, that maps to input$myInput (easy)
2 - When I change this input, change an output variable (which could be free form html/json/whatever) output$myOutput
3 - At this point, javascript on client side activates (say after you click myOutput 3 times), does some lookup and change input$myInput (shiny binding breaks!)
4 - Shiny now looks at the new value of input$myInput and provides a new output ouput$myOutput

Step 3 is where things get tricky. When I tried with simple experiments, shiny binding breaks and then we can no longer do step 4. There is a way I noticed somewhere where we could unbind all and then bind it all back. I also noticed that there are some new experimental features. What is the best way of going about this?

Thanks,

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server - versions, problems with libraries, etc.
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server - versions, problems with libraries, etc.
messages.body_plain:
I'm guessing when you run R on the Shiny Server machine and see that those libraries are there, you're running as your usual user account, and thus those libraries are in your personal library (~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0 or something). By default, Shiny Server launches R under the "shiny" user account. You need to either install those packages for everyone, or for the shiny user account.

If you have "sudo" access on the machine, you can do this to install for everyone:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('rgdal', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

Or this to install as the shiny user:

sudo su - shiny -c R
(then from the R prompt:)
install.packages('rgdal', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')

messages.subject: for reference: radioButtons with TRUE/FALSE as.logical workaround
messages.subject_clean: for reference: radioButtons with TRUE/FALSE as.logical workaround
messages.body_plain:
In ui.R, I had a checkboxInput:

    checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE)

In server.R, I had:

    df <- read.csv(input$dataset$datapath, 'header'=input$header, 'sep'=input$sep, 'quote'=input$quote)

Then I changed the checkboxInput to a radioButtons:

    radioButtons(
      'header'
      , 'Header:'
      , 'choices' = c('Yes' = TRUE, 'No' = FALSE)
      , 'selected' = 'Yes'
    )

and it wasn't working anymore.

A bit of testing showed that input$header was returning "TRUE" as opposed to just TRUE, i.e. radioButtons wraps TRUE with double quotes.

So here is the workaround I used: wrap input$header with as.logical

    df <- read.csv(input$dataset$datapath, 'header'=as.logical(input$header), 'sep'=input$sep, 'quote'=input$quote)

Feel free to chime in if there was a better, more elegant way.

Is the difference in behaviour intentional? Why aren't radioButtons called radiobuttonsInput and/or checkboxInput called checkBox, for consistency, or is the difference in naming convention reflecting the difference in behaviour with the logicals?

messages.body_plain:
For checked-boxes there are only two possible outcomes so it's natural to return boolean values TRUE and FALSE. For RadioButtons there can be more than 2 possible values so it's more natural to represent them using strings, hence "TRUE" and "FALSE".

>
> and it wasn't working anymore.
>
> A bit of testing showed that input$header was returning "TRUE" as opposed to just TRUE, i.e. radioButtons wraps TRUE with double quotes.
>

messages.subject_clean: Shiny server cannot find custom location for R installation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Allison,

If you set an environment variable named "R" to the path of the R binary you wish Shiny Server to run before starting the server (for instance, in /etc/init.d/shiny-server, or /etc/init/shiny-server.conf) Shiny Server should respect that and run the appropriate version of R.

We have this feature on our TODO list for inclusion in the config file, however, so users could use different versions of R for different locations or applications. It may take us a while to get to that feature, however.

Jeff

> Alison Link
> November 15, 2013 at 8:58 PM

> I've got the same setup: I've been testing my app on Glimmer, and am trying to now deploy it on a Shiny server on a VM at work running Red Hat OS.  When I check "which R" on my work VM, it points to /usr/bin/R, where I've got R 3.0.1 running.  Unfortunately, I'm noticing my CSV data isn't reading in the same way as it is on Glimmer (which looks like it's running R 2.15.3).  So, I'm trying to add a separate install of R 2.15.3 on my work VM to see if the R version discrepancy is what's causing the problem.
>

renderTable uses the xtable package to convert the data frame into an HTML table. Look into the sanitize argument of xtable, that allows you to pass verbatim HTML, as required for Mathjax.

On Monday, November 18, 2013 8:40:00 AM UTC-5, Andreas Recktenwald wrote:
> Hi, i have a question concerning Shiny and Mathjax, too. Is it possible to use Mathjax in tables ?
>
> "Stand-Alone" equations are rendered correctly, I added just for testing purposes 'HTML('\\( \\omega = \\zeta \\)' )" in the "ui.R" and it works. However, if I use renderTable and tableOutput it doesn't.
>
> Also using R Markdown produces correct result. Any ideas how I can solve this issue?
>

messages.subject_clean: redesigning the AMA cv risk calculator as R Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
When controversy about the American Medical Association's cardiovascular risk calculator made the news <http://www.nytimes.com/2013/11/18/health/risk-calculator-for-cholesterol-appears-flawed.html> a few days ago, I decided to check out the "online" calculator for myself. I was surprised to learn that the "online" calculator is simply an Excel file that is available online for download <http://my.americanheart.org/professional/StatementsGuidelines/PreventionGuidelines/Prevention-Guidelines_UCM_457698_SubHomePage.jsp>.

I've been wanting to learn how to create an R Shiny app for a while now, so I figured I would see if I could redesign the Excel calculator in R and deploy on my new beta Shiny hosted account. I think I am making some basic mistakes (probably related to reactive) that are giving me alternating errors when trying to view here <http://spark.rstudio.com/babymonitor/statin/>: "ERROR: argument is missing, with no default" and "Shiny couldn't find any UI for this application".

I put the code on github <https://github.com/ericpgreen/cvrisk> if anyone has time to take a look and offer feedback.

Thanks
Eric

messages.subject: Re: centering cells within a call to renderGvis from the GoogleVis package
messages.subject_clean: centering cells within a call to renderGvis from the GoogleVis package
messages.body_plain:
gvisTable doesn't look like it supports an align option through the Shiny interface. I just recently learned through another post in this group how to do some customization to a gvisTable through css.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/UCqfb2ocaEE

For your case, in ui.R try using:

tags$style(type="text/css", HTML("#data td { text-align: center}")), htmlOutput("data")

On Tuesday, November 19, 2013 11:17:49 AM UTC-5, Patrick Toche wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I have a simple shiny app that calls renderGvis from the GoogleVis package, to display a data table.
>
> By default the cells are right-aligned. I'd like to center them.
>
> The following intuitive syntax doesn't work:
>
> output$data <- renderGvis({
>   gvisTable(Data()$df, options = list('align'="center"))
> })
>
> The following setting in my ui.R should work:
>
> tags$head(
>   tags$style(type='text/css'
>     , ".google-visualization-table-td-number {text-align: center;}"
>   )
> )
>
> but it doesn't. Using "inspect element" I find that the following setting from table.css overrides my custom setting :
>
> .google-visualization-table-td-number {
>   text-align: right;
>   white-space: nowrap;
> }
>
> I can change right to center using the "inspect element" tool of the browser, but I can't control it within shiny.
>
> Any suggestions?
>
> Many thanks.
>

There is a (not currently documented, but we're most likely going to keep supporting it indefinitely) function "Shiny.onInputChange(name, value)" that you can call from JS, and in server.R, input$name will reflect that change and reactivity will be triggered, etc. (You appear to have the d3/JS chops to take it from there, but if not, let me know and I will try to help connect the dots for you...) messages.subject: Output reacting on dynamically created sliderInput change
messages.subject_clean: Output reacting on dynamically created sliderInput change
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to create Shiny application, which consists of a selectInput control, dynamically created sliderInput, some static input data and output data.

There are dependencies between elements of this app:
1. slider value depends on select list value
2. output data depends on slider value and select list value

(Please see attached scripts)

Because of those dependencies, I cannot get recalculation of output data right.

There are 2 options, that I've tried:
1. make output data reactive to slider value change
2. make output data reactive to both slider and select list values change

but:
1. output won't refresh in case slider recalculation (triggered by select list change) returns the same value, as before recalculation (see change from 'vec1' to 'vec2' - slider is recalculated (max boundary changes), but 'value' stays the same)
2. output will recalculate twice if both slider and select list value change (see change from 'vec1' to 'vec3')

Is there any way to trigger output recalculation whenever slider is recalculated even if it's value after recalculation is unchanged?
Or maybe there's another solution to my problem?

I would be very grateful for any suggestions,
Katarzyna

Gunnar,

Thanks for pointing that out. I'm going to log that as a bug.

In Shiny Server Pro, it's required that you run the shiny-server process as root in order to properly collect metrics for the admin interface, so we shouldn't be emitting that warning. You should indeed be running shiny-server as root, and then have a "run_as" directive to specify that Shiny apps should be run as the Shiny user.

Sorry for the misleading log message.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Output reacting on dynamically created sliderInput change
messages.subject_clean: Output reacting on dynamically created sliderInput change
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to summarize the philosophy behind this situation. Let me write my thoughts here.

a) There's an output object  output$out = f(input$x, y())  constructed from an input object  input$x  and a reactive conductor y()
b) The input object input$x is created through a dynamic UI  output$ui_x = g(y()) constructed from the reactive conductor y()

Thus :

 1) If we don't isolate anything, output$out is updated twice : firstly when y() is updated, but once y() is updated,the dynamic UI output$ui_x is updated and it creates a new input$x, thus output$out is updated a second time
 2) If we isolate by doing output$out = f(input$x, isolate(y())), then there's a problem in case (*) : the case when y() changes but not g(y())

The idea behind 2) is that, although y() is isolated, the value of y() will be read whenever input$x will be updated. But in case (*), input$x is not updated, and then output$out is calculated with the "old" value of y().

Thus my idea was to "anticipate" case (*) : when the reactive value value_has_not_changed[["x"]] is updated, it means that we are in case (*), and then defining output$out = f(input$x, isolate(y()), value_has_not_changed[["x"]] ) does the job.

Hi Dan,

I spent a bit of time in the jQuery datatables documentation (datatables.net/ <http://datatables.net/>) and I managed to put this together.

First, to suppress the global search box I added the following CSS in my mainPanel() in the ui.R script:

tags$head(
tags$style(type="text/css", ".dataTables_filter {display: none;    }"
)

Then, I added "bLengthChange=F" as an option in the renderDataTable function in the server.R script.

There may be better ways to do this.

I'm still trying to figure out how to remove the column filtering at the bottom of the table. I can see how this would be useful with large tables, but with small tables (where you see everything in one page) it is less important and takes up too much visual space.

Hope this helps.

K.

messages.subject: Re: suppress records per page dropdown and search box in data tables

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I also wanted to get rid of the column filter elements at the bottom and your answer gave me an idea. Below is a minimal example how to obtain a stripped down DataTable with some custom column sizes.

library(shiny)

runApp(
  list(
    server=function(input, output, session) {

      output$customtable = renderDataTable({
        mtcars},
        options=list(iDisplayLength=5,                    # initial number of records
                     aLengthMenu=c(5,10),                  # records/page options
                     bLengthChange=0,                       # show/hide records per page dropdown
                     bFilter=0,                                    # global search box on/off
                     bInfo=0,                                      # information on/off (how many records filtered, etc)
                     bAutoWidth=0,                            # automatic column width calculation, disable if passing column width via aoColumnDefs
                     aoColumnDefs = list(list(sWidth="300px", aTargets=c(list(0),list(1))))    # custom column size
                    )
      )
    },

    ui=basicPage(
      tagList(
        singleton(
          tags$head(
            tags$style(type="text/css", "tfoot {display:none;}")
            )
          )
        ),
       dataTableOutput('customtable')
    )
  )
)

Regards,

T.

If I am interacting with the app, I have not seen this happen. If I leave it idle in the browser, however, it may (but not always) gray out. It works again on refresh. I thought maybe Spark has some kind of inactivity time out feature that is somewhat new, since I have never seen this happen before and I have many times had apps open in my browser for very long periods of time without issue. But I also noticed that the gray out does not always happen, and when it does, it can be 45 seconds after loading the app and leaving it idle, or after five minutes, or 15 minutes. It is highly variable. My last observation is that it does not seem to happen on our self-hosted shiny server, only on Spark. Though, with the intermittent nature of the gray out, it is hard to know for sure.

Here is an example of three log files on Spark from two runs of the app, the first where it does not gray out and I close the connection myself by exiting the browser, and the second and third where I get the gray out:

messages.subject_clean: Leaflet and Shiny - Color Control of Shapes
messages.body_plain: Hi Aaron, without seeing the rest of your code, my guess is that your data.frame converts the color strings into factors. When Shiny passes the parameters onto the Leaflet library, this finds no valid colors and uses the default black value. To supress this behaviour you could use stringsAsFactors = FALSE when constructing your data.frame. Below is a reproducible example. Not the prettiest R code, but might be useful to someone. library(shiny) library(leaflet) library(RColorBrewer) library(plyr) runApp( list( server=function(input, output, session) { # create the map map <- createLeafletMap(session, 'map') # create some points DF <- data.frame( lat = c(52.4912694, 49.04323, 49.04323), lon = c(13.292079, 13.49518, 8.39053), id = c("A","B","C"), myVar = runif(3,100,400), color = c(brewer.pal(3,"Set3")) , stringsAsFactors = FALSE) radiusFactor <- 10000 observe({ if(input$drawPoints == 0) { return(NULL) } else { map$clearShapes() # get data into a nested list with the dlply function. paramList <- dlply(DF, 2, function(x) { list(x[['lat']], x[['lon']], x[['myVar']]*radiusFactor/ max(12, input$map_zoom)^2, x[['id']], list(weight = 1.2, # stroke weight fill = T, # fill object color = '#808080', # stroke color, grey opacity = 0.9, # stroke opacity fillColor = x[['color']], # fill color fillOpacity = 0.7, # fill opacity clickable = T) )}) # call lapply with custom wrapper function to map$addCircle. # the names of the list have to be stripped before being sent to map$addCircle lapply(paramList, function(x) do.call(map$addCircle, unname(x))) } }) }, ui=basicPage( mainPanel( leafletMap("map", "100%", 550, initialTileLayer = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png ", initialTileLayerAttribution = HTML('© OpenStreetMap contributors, CC-BY-SA'), options = list(center = c(51.01, 8.68), zoom = 6, maxZoom = 10, minZoom=4, maxBounds = list(list(30,-20),list(68,90)))), actionButton("drawPoints", "Draw")) )) ) Regards, Tudor Am Donnerstag, 21. messages.subject: Re: select row in DataTable
messages.subject_clean: select row in DataTable
messages.body_plain:
Yes, it is possible.

The main problem with binding data tables is sorting/filters/pagination. When a user sorts table, a row number is returned from a sorted table, which makes returning row index useless. Filters and pagination do not make life any easier. The most painless solution I can think of is returning all the contents of the row, not just the row number and matching it with your data frame in R. Obviously, all entries would have to be unique.

I have attached a working example that returns an entire selected row as a character vector. You can also uncomment
//return $(tbl).children().children('.rowsSelected').index() + 1; in DTbinding.js
if you want a row number instead.

Cheers.

Updated: Made a mistake in a post above (deleted). Updated file attached

messages.subject_clean: Newbee - Shiny on Mac OS X
messages.body_plain:
I stick the following at the top of all my scripts that require knowing the current directory, e.g. when saving data or plots, etc..

# set working directory
  if(.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
    setwd("c:/R/shiny")
  } else {
    setwd("~/R/shiny")
  }

I have used the above on Windows, Mac OSX and Ubuntu. Naturally, adapt the directory structure to yours.

You may want to read about the .Renviron (aka Renviron.site) and about the rsession.conf, which store your default settings.

I use the following (add/remove the # depending on platform):

# Windows .Renviron
# RSTUDIO_PDFLATEX = "C:/texlive/2013/bin/win32"
# R_LIBS_USER = "C:/R/library"
# R_USER = "C:/R"
# R_DOC_DIR = "C:/R"
# HOME = "C:"

# Linux Renviron.site
# R_LIBS_USER = "~/R/library"
# R_USER = "~/R"
# R_DOC_DIR = "~/R"
# HOME = "/home/patrick" # not needed

# MacOSX Renviron.site
 R_LIBS_USER = "~/R/library"
 R_USER = "~/R"
 R_DOC_DIR = "~/R"
# HOME = "/Users/PatrickToche" # not needed

# If there are multiple versions of the same package,
# the local library is searched first:
 R_LIBS_SITE=${R_LIBS_SITE-'/usr/local/lib/R/site-library:/usr/lib/R/site-library:/usr/lib/R/library'}

# By default RStudio sets the R_LIBS_USER environment variable to ~/R/library.

messages.subject: Re: Gray-out in Firefox
messages.subject_clean: Gray-out in Firefox
messages.body_plain:
Matt,

Thanks for reporting this, with such good investigation.

Did you notice that this started happening very recently (in the past week)? If so, I think you have actually pointed to a problem, and we will look into that very soon.
If that has always happened, could you please point me to your application(s) so we take closer look.

But to answer your question, by default the sessions do not time out as long as there is an open connection, and that is the behavior you see in your local server. On spark and glimmer servers we have setup a session limit which should apply to some applications, but not all.

Hope this helps, and we will let you know when we have an update on the issue.

Fereshteh

messages.subject_clean: How to use accent in shiny server?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

Problem (partially) solved !

Thanks to shiny app of Laurent ( https://gist.github.com/stla/7144955 ) I realised that sessionInfo() in R, sessionInfo() inside a shiny app called locally, and sessionInfo() inside a shiny App delivered through shiny-server do NOT give the same answer regarding to locale ! R and local shiny are OK (give UTF-8) but shiny server give the single value of "C"...

After reading this : http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/locales.html  i added to the top of the server.R file this instruction :

Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "fr_FR.UTF-8")

and it works (partially) normally, at least ! I say partially because if I stop/start my shiny-server the problem of the accentued variable at lines 40 and 41 remains until I take the accent over. BUT, if I call the app once in it(s corrected way, and then reput the accents in the var names at lines 40 and 41 of server.r, it work perfectly... So it acted like the Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "fr_FR.UTF-8") was not taking into account since the code is not readed once fully, and then it's ok.

I tried before Sys.setenv(LANG="fr_FR.UTF-8") and options(encoding="UTF-8") but without success.

So now the question is : how can I do to set this definitively to all the apps running on my shiny-server without beeing obliged to add this at the top of all apps ?

Thanks for advises.

Grégoire

messages.subject: Creating a Shiny Server package for Arch Linux
messages.subject_clean: Creating a Shiny Server package for Arch Linux
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I've started to put together a shiny-server-git package for Arch Linux to be submitted to the AUR <https://aur.archlinux.org/>:

    https://github.com/khughitt/pkgbuild/tree/master/shiny-server

I think I'm getting pretty close but have run into a couple issues trying to launch the server.

The first problem relates to the location of the node-posix package and is similar to that experienced by another user on the list <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/posix/shiny-discuss/YdFGLnJy_vs/gdtHaTdkkqoJ>:

> $ shiny-server
>
> module.js:340
>     throw err;
>           ^
> Error: Cannot find module '../../build/Release/posix'
>     at Function.Module._resolveFilename (module.js:338:15)
>     at Function.Module._load (module.js:280:25)
>     at Module.require (module.js:364:17)
>     at require (module.js:380:17)
>     at Object.<anonymous> (/usr/local/shiny-server/lib/core/fsutil.js:16:13)
>     at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
>     at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
>     at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
>     at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
>     at Module.require (module.js:364:17)

The work-around suggested in the above-mentioned thread seems to resolve the issue:

> git clone  https://github.com/melor/node-posix.git
> npm build node-posix
> sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/shiny-server/build/Release/
> sudo mv node-posix /usr/local/shiny-server/build/Release/posix

However, now a different issue is now encountered when attempting to launch the server:

> $ shiny-server
> [2013-11-25 14:46:11.641] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v0.4.0.0 (Node.js v0.10.21)
> [2013-11-25 14:46:11.643] [INFO] shiny-server - Using config file "/usr/local/shiny-server/config/default.config"
> [2013-11-25 14:46:11.673] [ERROR] shiny-server - Error loading config: Object #<Object> has no method 'getpwuid'
> [2013-11-25 14:46:11.674] [INFO] shiny-server - Shutting down worker processes

I don't have too much experience working with Node.js, so I'm a bit at a loss as to how to proceed from here.

Any suggestions?

Best,
Keith

messages.subject: Re: Using R's system() command with shiny-server on Linux
messages.subject_clean: Using R's system() command with shiny-server on Linux
messages.body_plain:
Keep in mind that by default shiny-server runs applications as the "shiny" user, who should be a low-privileged user. If sudo worked for that user without a password... *shudder*. Any security vulnerability in your app or in the Shiny stack would mean an attacker could totally own your machine!

If you must have some kind of high-privilege-requiring task kicked off by actions by users of Shiny apps, then try to have the Shiny app just add tasks to a queue of some kind, and have a higher-privileged process running and waiting for items to arrive in that queue. You could use something like rzmq <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rzmq/index.html>, or even just put files in a directory that the shiny user has write access.

)

messages.subject_clean: ShinySky -- A collection of Shiny UI components/widgets!!
messages.body_plain:
Introducing ShinySky -- A collection of Shiny UI components/widgets that are not a part of standard Shiny.

Currently there is only styled buttons and alerts in ShinkySky, but the aim is to slowly add to it so that it becomes at "feature-parity" with Bootstrap, i.e. using standard R idiom, functions, one can completely define everything there is in Bootstrap.

The intention is also to collate together the various components being customised by the good people in this forum and condense it into this one package for all to use!

Get started with the example

> install.packages("devtools") # if not already installed
> devtools::install_github("ShinySky","AnalytixWare")
> #require(shinysky)
> shinysky::run.shinysky.example()

Welcomes contribution on Github

> https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky

 <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-k5tktWE5dcI/UpYpA_e_jwI/AAAAAAAADhY/QppyXTNAjcw/s1600/Untitled.png>

> On Saturday, September 14, 2013 3:19:53 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > MM2, it has to do with connections where websockets cannot be successfully used. Shiny Server uses SockJS which provides a websocket-like interface that is either implemented using actual websockets if possible, and if not, then it falls back to emulating websockets using older technologies such as XmlHttpRequest.
> >
> > We tag each SockJS connection with a unique token, this is for security related reasons that are not really worth getting into. If we see a given token more than once, previously we were rejecting the second and subsequent attempts to use the token. But in your cases the token was legitimately getting sent >1 times because the websocket was partially but not fully successful--it succeeded enough to redeem the token but not enough that SockJS considered the connection usable. So the fix I implemented is to allow tokens to be reused.

messages.subject_clean: Grey out for multiple pages (maybe SocketJS token generation problem)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I have a problem, and I think that with everyone, who are working with multiple pages (yourapp/www/index.html without ui.R) in their app.

The app's first page is working, but others grey out before they are loaded.

I'am afraid that the problem occurs only with pages like: (http://spark.rstudio.com/yourapp/*.html).
For example when you type http://spark.rstudio.com/youraccount/yourapp/ in your browser, works like a charm, but http://spark.rstudio.com/youraccount/yourapp/index.html doesn't.

Pleae find an example error message below:

[Error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
http://spark.rstudio.com/medwatch/shiny/index.html__sockjs__/t=*/info

How can we fix SockJS token generation problem with multiple pages?

Any help would be highly appreciated.

With best wishes,

Laszlo

messages.subject_clean: ShinySky -- A collection of Shiny UI components/widgets!!
messages.body_plain:
GitHub

I guess the most ideal way is if you can fork my Github repository write your new component in your branch of the code and then do a pull request.

If you are unfamiliar with GitHub then this is the great place to get started https://help.github.com/set-up-git-redirect

Another way to contribute is to simply add an enhancement request by pressing the "New Issue" button on https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky/issues. You can paste the link to the component in there so that it's implementation will be on the radar.

Build package

Once you have fork the repository I recommend using RStudio IDE for building the packages as the build feature is built into RStudio.

http://www.rstudio.com/ide/docs/packages/overview

Simple Rules

The code in there are still quite simple so it shouldn't be too hard to learn from the code examples. But following these rules will be beneficial (http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#building-inputs)

Shiny input components should try to adhere to the following principles, if possible:
Designed to be used from HTML and R: Shiny user interfaces can either be written using R code (that generates HTML), or by writing the HTML directly. A well-designed Shiny input component will take both styles into account: offer an R function for creating the component, but also have thoughtfully designed and documented HTML markup.
Configurable using HTML attributes: Avoid requiring the user to make JavaScript calls to configure the component. Instead, it’s better to use HTML attributes. In your component’s JavaScript logic, you can easily access these values using jQuery <http://api.jquery.com/data/#data-html5> (or simply by reading the DOM attribute directly).

    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel(title="hello","hello",
        tabsetPanel(
          tabPanel(title="hi"),
          tabPanel(title="hi2")
        )
      ),
      tabPanel(title="wassup","wassup2",
               tabsetPanel(
                 tabPanel(title="hi3"),
                 tabPanel(title="hi4")
               )
      )
    )

messages.body_plain:
I have a dataset and I am practicing developing an application identical to: https://gist.github.com/wch/4034323

I am having difficulty imputing ranges, specifically for some sliders. I get the following error messages:

Listening on port 7219
Error in .subset2(x, i, exact = exact) :
  attempt to select less than one element
Error in if (min(value) < min) stop(paste("slider initial value", value,  :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I understand that I haven't plugged in the ranges yet, but have tried many combinations without getting it to function. Looking for a little guidance regarding where/how they might be able to put in. For the variables, the ranges are:
"Age" = 19-100
"Duration of Bacteremia (days)" = 1-15
"Length of Stay (days)" = 3-2363 (the max is an outlier, otherwise, the max ecluding this value is 750)

Here is the server and ui coding:

ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia at SFGH"),

  sidebarPanel(

    wellPanel(
      selectInput(inputId = "x_var",
                  label = "X variable",
                  choices = c("Age" = "age",
                              "Duration of Bacteremia (days)" = "bact_dura",
                              "Length of Stay (days)" = "los"),
                  selected = "Age"
      ),

      uiOutput("x_range_slider")
    ),

    wellPanel(
      selectInput(inputId = "y_var",
                  label = "Y variable",
                  choices = c("Age" = "age",
                              "Duration of Bacteremia (days)" = "bact_dura",
                              "Length of Stay (days)" = "los"),
                  selected = "Age"
      ),

      uiOutput("y_range_slider")
    ),

    checkboxInput(inputId = "sex",
                  label = "Separate men/women",
                  value = FALSE),

    wellPanel(
      p(strong("Model predictions")),
      checkboxInput(inputId = "mod_linear",    label = "Linear (dot-dash)"),
      checkboxInput(inputId = "mod_quadratic", label = "Quadratic (dashed)"),
      checkboxInput(inputId = "mod_loess",     label = "Locally weighted LOESS (solid)"),
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = "input.mod_loess == true",
        sliderInput(inputId = "mod_loess_span", label = "Smoothing (alpha)",
                    min = 0.15, max = 1, step = 0.05, value = 0.75)
      )
    )
  ),

  mainPanel(
    plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot"),

    conditionalPanel("input.mod_linear == true",
                     p(strong("Linear model")),
                     verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "mod_linear_text")
    ),

    conditionalPanel("input.mod_quadratic == true",
                     p(strong("Quadratic model")),
                     verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "mod_quadratic_text")
    ),

    conditionalPanel("input.mod_loess == true",
                     p(strong("LOESS model")),
                     conditionalPanel("input.sex == true",
                                      p("Note: categorical variable ", code("sex"),
                                        " cannot be used as a predictor in a LOESS model.",
                                        " (The plot above uses two separate models.)")
                     ),
                     verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "mod_loess_text")
    )

  )
))

server.R

library(ggplot2)

proj <- read.csv("245 Staph Database_251D.csv")

# Returns a logical vector of which values in `x` are within the min and max
# values of `range`.
in_range <- function(x, range) {
  x >= min(range) & x <= max(range)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  limit_data_range <- function() {
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Because we're using reactiveUI for x_range and y_range, they start
    # out as null, then get resolved after the client and server talk a bit.
    # If they are not yet set, there will be some errors in this function, so
    # do nothing for now (this function will be run again).
    if (is.null(input$x_range) || is.null(input$y_range)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Limit range of data
    # Take a subset of the data, respecting the limited range
    proj_sub <- proj[in_range(hw[[input$x_var]], input$x_range) &
                   in_range(hw[[input$y_var]], input$y_range), ]

    proj_sub
  }

  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({

    # Take a subset of the data, respecting the limited range
    proj_sub <- limit_data_range()

    if (is.null(proj_sub))
      return()

    # Get the x and y values from the non-range-limited data, for convenience
    xdat <- proj[[input$x_var]]
    ydat <- proj[[input$y_var]]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Make the base plot

    # If any models are drawn, make the points less prominent
    if (input$mod_linear || input$mod_quadratic || input$mod_loess)
      point_alpha <- 0.5
    else
      point_alpha <- 1

    # Separate by sex, if requested
    if (input$sex) {
      aes_mapping <- aes_string(x = input$x_var, y = input$y_var,
                                colour = "sex", shape = "sex")

      # Use different point geom specification, depending on if we're separating
      # by sex.
      points <- geom_point(solid = FALSE, alpha = point_alpha)

    } else {
      aes_mapping <- aes_string(x = input$x_var, y = input$y_var)

      # Use different point geom specification, depending on if we're separating
      # by sex.
      points <- geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = point_alpha)
    }

    # Base plot
    p <- ggplot(proj_sub, mapping = aes_mapping) +
      points +
      theme_bw() +
      scale_colour_hue(l = 40) +
      scale_shape(solid = FALSE) +
      # # Show the original range
      scale_x_continuous(limits = range(xdat)) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = range(ydat))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # If the range has been limited, draw lines displaying the limits

    if (max(input$x_range) != max(xdat)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = max(input$x_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }
    if (min(input$x_range) != min(xdat)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = min(input$x_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }

    if (max(input$y_range) != max(ydat)) {
      p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = max(input$y_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }
    if (min(input$y_range) != min(ydat)) {
      p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = min(input$y_range), linetype = "dashed",
                          alpha = 0.3)
    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Add model lines

    if (input$mod_linear) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, size = 0.75,
                           linetype = "dotdash")
    }
    if (input$mod_quadratic) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x + I(x^2),
                           size = .75, linetype = "dashed")
    }
    if (input$mod_loess) {
      p <- p + geom_smooth(method = loess, se = FALSE, linetype = "solid",
                           span = input$mod_loess_span)
    }

    print(p)
  })

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create renderUI sliders for x and y range, because their limits
  # depend on the selected x and y variables.

  output$x_range_slider <- renderUI({
    xmin <- floor(min(proj[[input$x_var]]))
    xmax <- ceiling(max(proj[[input$x_vary]]))

    sliderInput(inputId = "x_range",
                label = paste("Limit range"),
                min = xmin, max = xmax, value = c(xmin, xmax))
  })

  output$y_range_slider <- renderUI({
    ymin <- floor(min(proj[[input$y_var]]))
    ymax <- ceiling(max(proj[[input$y_var]]))

    sliderInput(inputId = "y_range",
                label = paste("Limit range"),
                min = ymin, max = ymax, value = c(ymin, ymax))
  })

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Functions for creating models and printing summaries

  make_model <- function(model_type, formula, ...) {
    # Get the subset of the data limited by the specified range
    proj_sub <- limit_data_range()
    if (is.null(proj_sub))
      return()

    # In order to get the output to print the formula in a nice way, we'll
    # use do.call here with some quoting.
    do.call(model_type, args = list(formula = formula, data = quote(proj_sub), ...))
  }

  output$mod_linear_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, "~", input$x_var)

    # Use sex as a predictor variable
    if (input$sex) {
      formula <- paste(formula, " * sex", sep = "")
    }

    summary(make_model("lm", formula))
  })

  output$mod_quadratic_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, " ~ ", "I(", input$x_var, "^2) + ",
                     input$x_var, sep = "")

    # Use sex as a predictor variable
    if (input$sex) {
      formula <- paste(formula, " * sex", sep = "")
    }

    summary(make_model("lm", formula))
  })

  output$mod_loess_text <- renderPrint({
    formula <- paste(input$y_var, "~", input$x_var)
    summary(make_model("loess", formula, span = input$mod_loess_span))
  })

})
